tints-shades-generator.quickAnswer: Tints mix your color with white; shades mix it with black. From #336699, a 50% tint is #99B3CC (each channel moves halfway to 255: 51 -> 153, 102 -> 179, 153 -> 204) and a 50% shade is #1A334D (each channel halves: 51 -> 26, 102 -> 51, 153 -> 77). The tool builds four tints and four shades at even 20% steps around your base.
keyFacts: Tint = base mixed with white; shade = base mixed with black.
A 50% tint moves every channel halfway to 255; a 50% shade halves every channel.
Design systems typically use 4-5 tints for backgrounds and 3-4 shades for text.
Even steps (20, 40, 60, 80%) make the scale feel smooth and predictable.
Tints keep the hue; shades keep the hue too - only lightness changes.
howTo: Enter your base color with the picker or a HEX code like #336699.
The tint row (toward white) and shade row (toward black) appear instantly.
Tap any swatch to copy its HEX.
Use tints for backgrounds, borders and hover states.
Use shades for headings, body text and pressed states.
tints-shades-generator.workedExample:
#336699 at 50% tint and 50% shade:
1. Tint: move each channel halfway to 255.
2. R: 51 + (255 - 51) x 0.5 = 153 -> 99 in hex.
3. G: 102 + (255 - 102) x 0.5 = 178.5, rounded 179 -> B3.
4. B: 153 + (255 - 153) x 0.5 = 204 -> CC. Tint = #99B3CC.
5. Shade: halve each channel: 25.5 -> 26 (1A), 51 (33), 76.5 -> 77 (4D). Shade = #1A334D.
6. The tool shows these at even 20% steps: 20/40/60/80 tints and shades.
benefits: A complete, even scale from one brand color in seconds.
Tints and shades never clash with the base - same hue throughout.
Perfect for building design-system color ramps.
One tap copies any step into your CSS.
limitations: Even RGB steps are not perceptually even - mid steps can look bunched.
Very dark shades may be indistinguishable from black in print.
Text on mid tints often fails contrast - check before shipping.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a tint, a shade and a tone?
faqs.a: A tint mixes the color with white, a shade mixes it with black, and a tone mixes it with gray. This tool generates tints and shades; tones sit between the two rows.
Even steps make the scale predictable: each swatch is visibly distinct from its neighbors without big jumps. Design systems commonly document colors at similar intervals.

faqs.q: How do I use these in a design system?
faqs.a: Name them by step (e.g. blue-20 to blue-80), use light tints for surfaces, the base for primary actions, and dark shades for text.

faqs.q: Can tints replace a separate light-mode palette?
faqs.a: Often yes - tints of your brand color at 10-20% make excellent light-mode backgrounds that stay on-brand.

faqs.q: Do shades work for dark mode?
faqs.a: Yes - deep shades (60-80%) of brand colors make great dark-mode surfaces, with the base color reserved for accents.
Not exactly - RGB mixing is linear but human vision is not. The steps are mathematically even, which is the standard, predictable approach.
